test_title: PYST 73: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which regulatory provisions did the the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) reference while imposing the fine on Acko General Insurance for violations related to outsourcing and commissions in May 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Section 40(1) of Insurance Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** took regulatory action against **Acko General Insurance** in **May 2025** for violations concerning **outsourcing** and **commission** payments.
 
• **Section 40(1)** of the **Insurance Act, 1938** serves as a critical provision that prohibits the payment of **remuneration** or **reward** by way of **commission** to any person for soliciting or procuring insurance business in **India**, unless that person is an authorized **insurance agent** or an **insurance intermediary**.
 
• The investigation by **IRDAI** revealed that the insurer had entered into arrangements that resulted in payments exceeding the permissible **commission caps** or were directed toward entities not eligible under the regulatory framework.
 
• The fine was imposed because the **outsourcing** expenses were found to be a means of circumventing the statutory limits on **acquisition costs** and **expenses of management**. *Hence, the statement regarding Section 40(1) is correct.*
 
• This regulatory intervention emphasizes the necessity for **general insurance companies** to adhere strictly to the **Insurance Act** and **IRDAI regulations** to maintain market integrity and protect **policyholders'** interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI):**
 
 
• It is a **statutory body** formed under the **IRDAI Act, 1999**.
 
• The **headquarters** of the authority are located in **Hyderabad**, having moved from **New Delhi** in **2001**.
 
• Its primary mission is to regulate and promote the **insurance** and **reinsurance** industries in **India** while ensuring the **financial security** of the sector.
 
 
 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938:**
 
 
• This is the **foundational legislation** governing the insurance sector in **India**.
 
• It provides the **legal framework** for the **registration** of insurance companies, **investment** of assets, and the **prohibition** of rebates and unauthorized commissions.
 
• **Section 64V** of this Act specifically deals with the **assets and liabilities** of an insurer and the determination of the **solvency margin**.
 
 
 
• **Outsourcing Regulations:**
 
 
• Under the **IRDAI (Outsourcing of Activities by Indian Insurers) Regulations, 2017**, insurers are strictly prohibited from outsourcing **core functions** such as **underwriting**, **claims settlement**, and **compliance** functions.
 
• The regulations aim to ensure that insurers retain **effective control** over their operations and do not utilize outsourcing as a loophole to pay extra **commissions**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 40(1) Enforcement:** The enforcement of this section ensures that the **cost of insurance** does not escalate due to unregulated **payouts** to intermediaries, which ultimately benefits the **end consumer**.
 
• **Compliance Framework:** Every insurer must submit an **annual certificate** signed by the **CEO** and **Compliance Officer**, affirming that all **outsourcing** arrangements and **commission** payments are in line with the **statutory provisions**.
 
• **Penalties:** **IRDAI** has the power to impose **monetary penalties** ranging from **1 lakh** to **1 crore** rupees per day of continuing violation or cancel the **certificate of registration** under extreme circumstances.
